title: From Crisis to Prosperity: AI and Open Finance for Holistic Financial Health and Smart Future Planning
authors: Bukovski, K.; Jain, K.; Cummins, M.; Bowden, J.; Tetteh, G.K.; Lin, Z.
venue: FRIL White Paper Series, Financial Regulation Innovation Lab
tldr: Open Finance data combined with AI and machine learning enables a holistic financial health framework that replaces static credit scoring with dynamic, personalised, resilience-focused guidance for consumers.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional credit-score-centric frameworks rely on historical repayment data and demographic proxies, failing to capture consumers' full financial health. The COVID-19 pandemic and cost-of-living crises exposed deep vulnerabilities in reactive, one-dimensional risk models.
approach: Proposes a conceptual framework integrating Open Finance data with AI/ML for holistic financial health evaluation.
Presents a hierarchical financial needs framework inspired by Maslow's theory with three sequential optimisation layers.
Reviews clustering techniques applied to Open Finance data to identify customer persona archetypes.
Discusses data architecture using relational and graph-based schemas with temporal structuring.
Covers predictive modelling approaches including ensemble methods, LSTM, and GETS modelling.
Evaluates model explainability using SHAP and LIME for transparency and regulatory compliance.
Reviews privacy-preserving techniques including GANs, VAEs, and Bayesian inference for synthetic data generation.
Discusses stochastic modelling using Monte Carlo simulation and Geometric Brownian Motion.
findings: num: Only approximately 8% of UK adults currently receive financial advice.
num: Low financial resilience affects approximately one quarter of UK adults in 2022, equating to 12.9 million people.
num: Auto-enrolment policies raise cumulative retirement contributions by 4.1% of first-year annualised salary.
Eight distinct customer personas identified through clustering, each requiring tailored financial guidance strategies.
Soft goal setting in fintech apps causally increases individuals' savings rate.
Hybrid human-AI interaction yields better performance in interactive reasoning tasks than either human or AI alone.
